_readme: Editorial decisions applied on top of docs/syllabus.json by scripts/build_syllabus.py.
The source list (jlptgrammarlist.neocities.org) has no entry for を, the direct
object particle, at any level, and is missing こそあど, question words, adjective
conjugation, ましょう/ませんか and んです from N5. Its own changelog shows it was
assembled over 28 days in 2020 and sorted 'alphanumerically'. It is therefore used
as a starting skeleton and a source of sense-disambiguation glosses, not as a
syllabus authority. Scope decisions cross-checked against Bunpro, JLPT Sensei and
Shin Kanzen Master. Every deviation from the source is recorded here.

ことに.gloss: to my surprise / delight (speaker's reaction to what follows)
ことに.why: Source glossed this '-ly', which describes the unrelated adverbial 〜ことに. The pattern is 〜ことに(は) and mainstream references place it at N2, but it is kept at N3 here since the surrounding cluster is taught at N3.

が#1.gloss: marks the subject; singles out which one
が#1.why: Source gloss was 'as for (identifies something)', which is a gloss of は. Left uncorrected this produces a が page that contradicts the は page on the single most important contrast in beginner Japanese.

しか○○ない.gloss: only; nothing but (with material between しか and ない)
しか○○ない.why: Disambiguated from N3 しかない 'have no choice but', which is a different pattern.

ら見ると.gloss: judging from; seen from the standpoint of
ら見ると.why: The source's own term string is truncated -- it lists 'ら見ると', which is not a Japanese construction. The pattern is から見ると.

ばかり#2.why: Disambiguated from the N4 ばかり 'only; nothing but'. Same form, unrelated use: 三日ばかり vs 読んでばかりいる.

以上#1.gloss: or more; upwards of (after a quantity)
以上#1.why: Disambiguated from 以上 sense 2, the reason marker. Same form, unrelated uses; both pages sit together so the split is visible.

以上#2.gloss: now that; given that (reason -- once X is the case, naturally Y)
以上#2.why: The major N2 point of the two; drives the page's placement beside からには and 上は.

を限りに.gloss: as of ~; with ~ as the last time (本日を限りに閉店)
を限りに.why: Source gloss 'starting from' reads the pattern backwards. It marks a terminal boundary -- the final occasion -- and the new state follows only by implication.

n3:ということ.term: ということだ / とのことだ
n3:ということ.gloss: I hear that; word is that (reported information)
n3:ということ.why: The N3 entry duplicated the N4 nominaliser ということ. The genuine N3 point is the hearsay form, which is what the source's own gloss describes.

merge.why: Four source pages for one form. だろう/でしょう is a plain/polite alternation, and sense 1 vs 2 is falling vs rising intonation. Splitting them hides both relationships.

merge.gloss: it'd be better to (and, negated, better not to)
merge.why: Sense 2 is sense 1 negated. That is conjugation, not a second grammar point.

split.why: Two different particles sharing one gloss ('to'). They overlap for destination and diverge everywhere else; a single page cannot teach the difference it exists to teach.
